column3: Therefore, since we also have so great a cloud of witnesses surrounding us, let us lay aside every weight and the sin that so easily entangles, and let us run with endurance the race set before us,
looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of faith, who for the joy set before him endured a cross, despising shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
For consider the one who endured such hostility against himself from sinners, so that you may not grow weary and lose heart.
You have not yet resisted to the point of blood in your struggle against sin,
and you have forgotten the encouragement that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not regard lightly the Lord’s discipline, nor lose heart when reproved by him,
for the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and he scourges every son whom he receives.”
Endure for discipline. God deals with you as sons, for what son is there whom a father does not discipline?
But if you are without discipline, of which all have become sharers, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
Furthermore, we had our earthly fathers as disciplinarians and respected them. Shall we not much more be subject to the Father of spirits and live?
For they disciplined us for a few days as seemed best to them, but he does so for our benefit, so that we may share his holiness.
Now all discipline for the moment does not seem to be joy but sorrow, yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those trained through it.
Therefore strengthen the drooping hands and the weakened knees,
and make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame may not be put out of joint but rather be healed.
Pursue peace with everyone, and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord,
watching carefully so that no one falls short of the grace of God, so that no root of bitterness grows up and causes trouble and through it many are defiled,
so that no one is sexually immoral or profane like Esau, who for a single meal sold his own birthright.
For you know that even afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for repentance, although he sought it with tears.
For you have not come to something that can be touched and to blazing fire and darkness and gloom and storm,
and to the sound of a trumpet and a voice of words, which those who heard begged that no further word be spoken to them,
for they could not bear what was commanded: “Even if an animal touches the mountain, it shall be stoned.”
And so terrifying was the sight that Moses said, “I am terrified and trembling.”
But you have come to Mount Zion and the city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels in festal gathering,
and to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God, Judge of all, and to the spirits of righteous people made perfect,
and to Jesus, mediator of a new covenant, and to sprinkled blood that speaks better than Abel’s.
See that you do not refuse the one who speaks. For if those did not escape when they refused the one who warned them on earth, much less will we if we turn away from the one from heaven.
At that time his voice shook the earth, but now he has promised, saying, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also heaven.”
And the phrase “yet once more” indicates the removal of the things being shaken as things that have been made, so that the things not shaken may remain.
Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us have gratitude, through which we may serve God acceptably with reverence and awe,
for our God is a consuming fire.
